data.gender_notes: Nihal is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nihal means 'young' or 'youthful' in Sanskrit. In Hindu mythology, Nihal is the name of a powerful god associated with joy and vitality. This name is often given to baby boys to bless them with a joyful and youthful spirit. The name Nihal carries the meaning “Young, Joyful” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nihal usually hope their child will grow to embody young, joyful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Nihal belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Young, Joyful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nihal total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nihal carries an inherent sense of joy, liveliness, and vitality in Hindu culture. It is believed that a boy named Nihal will grow up to be full of life, radiating happiness and positivity wherever he goes. The name also evokes a sense of youthfulness, suggesting that the person born with this name will always have a youthful spirit and zest for life.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Nihal is associated with the deity of joy and youthfulness, often represented as a form of Lord Shiva or Lord Krishna. The name is believed to carry the blessings of these gods, who bestow upon the person named Nihal a joyful and vibrant spirit, free from pain and sorrow. It is also believed that the name Nihal helps to purify the mind and instills a sense of happiness and contentment, bringing one closer to the divine.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit word निहल (nihala), meaning 'night' or 'master of the night'. In Hindu mythology, Nihal is the name of a Yaksha, a supernatural being who rules over the night.

historical_references.reference: Nihal Shahi was the last Sikh ruler of the Shahi Dynasty, ruling from 1602 to 1630. He is also known as Nihal Chand and Nihal Singh. According to Sikh tradition, Nihal Shahi was a devout Sikh and was a contemporary of the fifth Sikh Guru, Arjan Dev.

Another reference to Nihal can be found in Hindu mythology, specifically in the Mahabharata. Nihal is mentioned as the name of a king of the Haihayas, a branch of the Yadava clan. He ruled in the eastern part of Bharatvarsha (India) during the Mahabharata war.
